The Recent Happenings Board is located inside the town entrance, and that's where you'll find information on all the important goings on in the area.

A thriving trade town can tumble into ruins fit for only wolves and bandits if neglected, and a backwater village can rise to become the shining center of a territory's economy if it has a few vigilant samurai to stand guard over it!

Fumio and I will wait here and look after Mai. Tadao knows we’re Old Guard. If they spot us, they’ll know the hideout’s somewhere in the area.
Travel to the town inn and try to gather as much information about the bounty hunters as you can. See if you can find out where they're keeping Yasuka.
I'll go right away.
Bounty hunters attacked us, too. They said there’s a reward on your heads.
Someone wants the Old Guard wiped out. Whoever killed Masahiro, they know we're going to try to get our revenge.
Tell them what happened, Mai.

step.title: Find information about the bounty hunters

dialogue.text: Ah, another new face in my inn! I must say, it's become quite busy ever since the shogun's death.
I hear there are many bounty hunters in the area. Any idea who they're looking for?
Oh, yes, lots of bounty hunters. Between you and me, they're a rather rough lot; I'd prefer not serve them but, well, business is business!
I'm not entirely sure who hired them or what they're looking for, but they've been wandering around the forests a lot. I'd stay out of their way if I were you.

choice.text: What does he know about Masahiro's murder?

dialogue.text: Why has it become so busy?

Now that the shogun's gone, people are starting to worry about what's going to happen. Everywhere I look people are packing up their belongings and moving to pastures new, or drowning their sorrows in sake.
Either way, most of them are coming here, even if they're just passing through.
What have people been saying about the shogun's death?

Oh, it’s all anyone’s talking about. A merchant, fresh off the road from the capital, told me the shogun was struck down with a fever and died that same night. Worse than that, there's talk that Masahiro's son has vanished too!
So unfortunate, and on the same day that Masahiro was due to celebrate his fifth year on the throne!

choice.text: I want to talk about something else.

dialogue.text: What do you think will happen now?
War, death, misery -- the usual. Honestly, you give those daimyo just a sniff of power and they become like starving dogs fighting over a rancid bone.
What can you tell me about the disappearance of Masahiro's son?

Only what I've been told, and that isn't much. Apparently, he vanished shortly after the shogun's retainers discovered Lord Masahiro had been murdered. I don't know where the boy could be now, but I hope he's safe.
Let's talk about something else.
Thanks. That's all I wanted to know.
Well, safe travels on the –
Hey, Shoji, does that ronin look familiar to you?
Not really. Why?
It's the same ronin that helped that fat Shira Tancho get away earlier. Yeah, I'm sure of it!
I think you’re right, Hachiro! Hey you, ronin. Where d'you think you're going?

choice.text: These bullies need to be taught a lesson!
I should try to be discreet.

dialogue.text: So you're the ones hunting the Shira Tancho. Mind if I ask who your boss is?
Heh heh! That's none of your damned business. All you need to know is that there's a price on your head – a price we're going to collect!

choice.text: I'll give them one more warning.

dialogue.text: Attacking me will be the stupidest thing you've done all day.
Gulp! N-now g-gentlemen, please refrain from any acts of violence in my –
There's no way you're going out that front door alive, ronin!
So, you want to fight? Come on then!
You scum kidnapped Yasuka, didn't you? You think picking on a lame old man makes you tough?
No, but it does make us rich. And we're just about to become a whole lot richer, once we cash in your head.
I think you have the wrong person, my friends.
Typical Shira Tancho... trying to wriggle out of a fight like a worm.
Da...damn. So st-strong. Guess we're not going to collect that reward after all...
Please! We give up! You wanna know where that crippled old guy is? You'll find him at the E Sukemoto Caves...

step.title: Return to the Old Guard Hideout

dialogue.text: You're back!
Oh, please tell me my father's okay!
They're keeping Yasuka in the E Sukemoto Caves. He's safe, for now.
I think I know where it is.
Then what are we waiting for?
Fumio, you stay here and look after Mai. I'll go with our friend here to rescue Yasuka.
Aye-aye, sir! I won't let any harm come to Mai.
Please be careful...
...Ah, it's Hiroshi's helper. How did you know I was here?
Yasuka!
And Satoshi, too. I haven't seen you at my inn for a while.
Mai was worried about you.
Ah, my darling daughter. She worries... too much.
Yasuka, are you hurt?
Not enough to stop me from walking. Don't worry.
We'll get you out of here. Stay close.
That sake you're drinking is dulling your edge, Satoshi. You fell into my trap.
Tadao, you bastard! I I thought you'd be hiding in the dark somewhere.
And miss out on the pleasure of killing my number one competitor? I don't think so.
I've been looking forward to this day for a long time.

choice.text: I don't want to fight him if I don't have to.
He'll pay for what he has done.

dialogue.text: Who's your master, Tadao? Who's ordering you to capture Old Guard members?
Gold's my master, ronin, nothing else. Gold to keep my rice bowl full and my head dry. Whose hand I take it from doesn't matter.
And my employers are paying me extremely well for every Old Guard corpse I bring them. You're not going anywh --
Ah, you must be Tadao. This note states that you have placed a bounty of three hundred coins on my head.
Quite a sum for one like mine.
Huh?! How did you get in here?
Through the front entrance of course.
Wh-what–?! But there were twenty guards outside!
Hmm... not any more.
Yuudai?! Hahaha! You old basket head, how you doing!
It has been a long time, Satoshi. Nice to see you.
Damn it all! Everyone, attack!
Tadao, let us leave here in peace. There's no need for more bloodshed.
Huh! Do I look like a priest to you? I get paid for bloodshed -- it's what I do.
You deserve no mercy for what you've done here, Tadao. Your cowardice has earned you your death!
Tsk... No, it has earned me my fortune.
Good timing there, Yuudai. Thanks for the assist.
My pleasure, Satoshi. It's nice to see you again. I had hoped to find you eventually.

choice.text: What made him change his mind?

dialogue.text: I thought you'd given up being a samurai. What made you change your mind?
This man Tadao sent bounty hunters to my home; I was forced to show them the error of their ways.
And then I realized: there can be no peace until the killers of Masahiro are brought to justice.
Nice to have you with us, Yuudai. Come on, let's get out of here
Guess who's back!
Satoshi!
Huh, Yuudai's here as well?
Ah, if it isn't Fumio. A pleasure to see you again.
Father!
My darling daughter!
Oh! Father, I thought I'd never see you again!
Didn't I tell you not to worry?
Thank you, everyone, for bringing my father back safely.
So all's well that ends well. I think this calls for a drink!
KWAA!
Eh? Oh -- Kinme!
Ain't that Hiroshi's bird?
She's carrying another letter. Let me read it out.

intro.text:
My friends of the Old Guard,
The young master is with me and we have reached the open road, but Shinmen sacrificed himself to ensure our escape.
His loss is a great blow to our clan that cannot be measured in words. I pray that his soul finds happiness in the afterlife.

dialogue.text: Wait just there! Did... did Hiroshi just tell us that Shinmen's dead too?!
It can't be true...
The loss of Shinmen will be sorely felt by all within the Shira Tancho.
Shinmen, you... you were the best of us... even if we didn't always see eye-to-eye.
Damn it! I We'll get the bastards who did this, I swear!
Hiroshi's written more. Should I keep reading?
Do it. Let's hear what else he has to say.

intro.text: Before he died, Shinmen told me that he was due to meet a contact with information on the plot to assassinate the Shogun.
They were due to meet on the fifth day of the Month of Water at the entrance of Masai Village.

If you can, travel there in Shinmen’s place to meet the contact and find out what he has learned. Fate willing, we will see each other again soon.
--H

dialogue.text: Shinmen sure wasn't short of ideas.
Heh... typical him.
So it looks like we've got our orders...

intro.label: label1

choice.text: Will Yasuka and Mai be okay?

dialogue.text: Yasuka, what will you do now?
As much as I wish I could go with you to avenge our lord and Shinmen, that run-in with the bounty hunters has taught me I'm no longer much use in a fight.
I wouldn't let you go anyway, father! From now on, I'm not letting you out of my sight.
Ha! Ha! There, my daughter has spoken! Sorry my friend, but our destiny lies elsewhere.
We'll travel south. We have friends who would be willing to hide us for a while. We won't be in any danger.
What do you know about Shinmen's mysterious contact?
Each of the Great Clans keeps its own cadre of ninja for spying and espionage duties. If Shinmen approached outsiders to help him, he must have suspected the Shira Tancho had been compromised.
I would have put money on Shinmen having something sneaky up his sleeve, that guy is... was... craftier than a two-headed fox.
So does that mean I'm coming with you?
Well, we can't let you wander the countryside alone, not now the bounty hunters think you're one of us.
Yeah, you'd better stick with us for now, pal. Besides, we could use a warrior like you!
Now, I figure we'd best get moving. The rendezvous is two days from now, and that doesn't give us much time.
Then here we must part ways. Mai and I will travel south, to my friend's inn. There we should be safe; I don't think anyone will try looking for us now.
Thank you for rescuing my father. Please, when all this horrible business has blown over and the land is at peace again, come visit us at our inn.
Will we get dumplings?
Of course! And for you, Fumio, I'll make them extra big!
Hee hee... th-thank you, Mai.
Ha! You've turned red as a strawberry, Fumio!
Wh-what?! Sh-shut up!
I wish you two the best for the future, Yasuka and Mai. Farewell!
If you come across any old guard on your travels, be sure to send them our way.
Find out what you can about where the bounty hunters are keeping Yasuka, then report back.
Don't worry. I won't let you down.
Let's head to E Sukemoto Caves to rescue Yasuka.
Eh? Oh, you're back already! Hmm, I don't see any of those mushrooms on you...
Hurry up and collect one. We'll be waiting for you here.
So... where's our contact?
You sure this is the place?
Yep, dead sure. Hiroshi's always spot-on when it comes to directions. The contact's got to be around here somewhere.
Say, uh, guys... does this look like blood to you, on this bush?

intro.text: You found a hidden path!

dialogue.text: It is, and not just on the bush. Look -- there's more behind it.
Not the sort of sign I was hoping for. Come on, let's see where it leads.
Urgh...
This man wears the uniform of a shinobi.
He's gotta be Shinmen's contact!
We were told to meet a man here who has information on the murder of Masahiro.
Fast... so fast... We never stood a chance
It's no use trying to talk to him, not in his condition. His wounds need treatment at once.
We can't leave this man's wounds untreated. We need to find him a healer.
You're right. Dead men tell no tales, and we need to get him on his feet again.
Then let us take him to the town.We are sure to find a healer there.
Right. Uh... say, are you well enough to travel? We're going to take you to a healer.
So fast... so fast...
Poor guy's delirious with pain. Come on, let's get him out of here.
Right, we need to find a healer quickly.
Uh... maybe try the inn?
Eh? Is that young man hurt? Here, Let me take a look at him.

choice.text: I don't like that creepy old guy.
If he can help us, we should let him.

dialogue.text: I recognize you!
Heh heh! Konichiwa my friend. Our paths cross yet again.
Hey, old geezer, do you even know what you're doing?
Of course I do! I've been helping farmers with their injured animals for years.
Urrrgh...
Sigh! That'll have to do. Go on, do what you can.
It's all pretty much the same really... spleen, lungs, heart, giblets, we've all got 'em. Now, let me see...
Hmm... puncture wounds, several deep, slashing cuts... tell me, young man, does it hurt when I do this?
Ouch!
And this?
Arrgh!
Fractured shoulder, too.
Can you heal him?
Youngster, I can heal just about anyone... provided I have the right tools.
This boy's injuries are serious. They'll need a special poultice to prevent infection and speed up healing.
And you've got this poultice on you, right?
Uh... no. I have most of the ingredients though, just missing a heaven's mercy mushroom.
It's a very rare example of its kind, and it grows only in the darkness of caves.
You'll need to retrieve one for me. Heh!

choice.text: I don't have time for errands.

dialogue.text: Isn't there something else you can do for him? We don't have time to run around forests picking mushrooms.
I could say a prayer to his ancestors, see if that works.
But I wouldn't bet my sandals on it.
Then let's get moving. Any idea where I can find one of these mushrooms?
They're rare but they're pretty easy to spot. They have large red caps with white mottling, slimy to the touch and they smell like sweaty sandals!
I think that's how they got their name - because it's the first thing you say when the smell hits your nose!
Hmm. Now that I think about it, I'm certain someone once told me they grow in the cave to the south.
I recommend you start your search there.
There's no point in all of us going. Fumio, Yuudai and I will wait here. We'll leave the rest to you, friend.
We'll take the ninja to the inn and try to get him comfortable.
Yes, that's a good idea. I won't be able to carry him there all by myself, not with my bad back.
Oh! And one warning before I forget: Once you find the mushroom and collect it, run - as fast as you can.
They're a delicacy to Oni; the scent drives them crazy with hunger.

choice.text: Oh, so now he tells me!

dialogue.text: Oni - those little blue monsters with the fangs? Yeesh! This just keeps getting better and better...
Heh! I never said it was going to be easy, youngster. Now, hurry up and get to it!
And watch out for the giant red Oni! Those monsters, they'll try to eat you soon as they see you - then use your bones for toothpicks!
Don't try to fight them whatever you do! Wait for them to fall asleep, then sneak past - carefully!
I can't believe I almost forgot to mention them! Heh, that's old age for you!
This man's life is in your hands now, friend
Look for us at the back room of the inn when you return.
Thanks for the warning. I should be okay.
Butt out of other people's business, old man.
Heh! You should learn to respect your elders, youngster. I'm just trying to be helpful.
Do whatever you can to save his life.
Stand aside, stand aside. I'll need plenty of room if I'm going to help him.
Remember what Kojuro said - Wait for the red oni to doze off before attempting to sneak past it.

step.title: Return to Kojuro with a heaven's mercy mushroom

dialogue.text: Ah-ha! So you're back, youngster. Still in one piece, too. Did you find the mushroom?
I have it right here. It wasn't easy avoiding all those Oni.
Heh! You did well, and I knew I was right to trust you.
Now, all I need to do is mash some up and rub it onto his wounds like so...
... add a dash of honeysuckle juice...
... some bamboo shavings...
... and finish it off with a nice tight bandage.
There, all done!
Hey! He's coming round!
P-please... my name is Kurai, of the Ka... Kagehito ninja clan.
Kurai, who did this to you?
A man... or the ghost of a man. He struck from the darkness, moved like smoke on the wind ...
But his blades cut like steel through new wheat, and he slew my companions before we sensed his presence.
I fled, to my eternal shame. It was all I could do, pow... powerless as I was to st-stop him.
The Kagehito? I've never heard of them.
Our clan prides itself on its anonymity. Few know of the Kagehito's existance.
They're something of a myth; an independent clan of shinobi, without allegiance to land or lord.
Your friend speaks the tru... truth. We answer only to the will of our jonin and never take sides, except to carry out the letter of our contract.
Kurai, we need to find the men responsible for the shogun's murder. Is there anything you can do to help us?
Other scouts might know more; my jonin sent more than one team into the forest. My team was meant to meet your friend Shinmen and guide him to our village.
You will have to travel to our village and meet our jonin. Alas, I am too injured to make the journey with you.
so take this: a kagehito talisman, to identify yourself to my clansmen who stand watch over our home. The Kagehito are hostile to outsiders, and they'll attack if you do not state your purpose.
Thank you, Kurai, for your assistance. We'll leave at once.
He's passed out, the poor young fellow. The pain must have been too much for him to handle.
Will Kurai be all right?
He's young. He'll heal quickly enough.
Then let Kurai rest. We'll go to the Kagehito village.
Let Kurai rest. We'll go to the Kagehito village right away.
You guys go ahead. I'll wait here with Kurai, see if he comes round.
Tell the jonin that Kurai's safe here and will need to be escorted back to his village. I'll follow you when I know he's in the Kagehito's care.
Catch up with us when you can, Satoshi.
So now we need to find the hidden entrance to the Kagehito village...
Those sneaky shinobi! What makes 'em so special that they need to hide themsel -
Hey, guys! I think I might have found it - check that bush over there!

intro.text: You found a hidden path!

dialogue.text: That's twice now you've spotted something, Fumio. Impressive.
Hee hee! Nuttin' gets past Fumio. Eyes like an eagle, me.
Well done there, Fumio. I'll lead from here.
Sure thing! Just say if you need my super-sharp senses again!
But not your modesty...
Hee hee!

intro.label: label1

dialogue.text: Good work. Now, you go first.
Gulp! B-but there might be traps an' stuff in there - sharp traps!
Then we should count ourselves fortunate to have your 'eagle eyes' with us, Fumio.
Sigh! yeah, and my big mouth...
Hold it right there! You try taking one step closer, trespasser, and I'll pin you to that tree with kunai!
Whoa there... wait just a second! Let's talk about this!
I don't know how you found your way here, but your journey ends now!

choice.text: I'll try to make her understand.

dialogue.text: Hey! Wait! I don't want -
No more words! Save your breath for fighting!
You're making a big -
Why won't you -
Don't try anything, ninja! I've not come here to fight.
At last - a friendly face! I've been traipsing about in these woods for hours.
Huff! Puff! You win, trespasser. You... you might as well just kill me. The shame of losing to a samurai is too great.

choice.text: I never intended to kill her.
Heh... let her deal with it.

dialogue.text: Quit being so dramatic. I have no intention of killing you.
Then you have no honor, coward! A true warrior fights to the death -- not an inch before! I am a true warrior, even if you are not!

choice.text: Ninja shouldn't tell samurai what to do!

dialogue.text: And a wise warrior doesn't shed blood needlessly. Mercy is a virtue just as important as skill with a blade.
But...
Fine. But if you don't intend to kill me, what reason do you have for coming here?
We need to speak to your jonin. A team of shinobi belonging to your clan has been attacked and Kurai, the only survivor, is grievously wounded and recuperating back in town.
Kurai!
My friend is looking after him in Masai Village. I need to speak to your Jonin at once.
But how do I know you're telling me the truth? You could be here on a mission from our enemies.
Here, take a look at this talisman; it was given to us by Kurai himself.
If you still do not believe us, send someone back to the village to speak with Kurai. We will wait here, and you may take our weapons.
No. I... I believe you. Please, you're free to enter our village.
I will go ahead and inform my jonin of your arrival.

choice.text: I'm glad she's listening to reason.
She should've listened to me before!

dialogue.text: Thank you for trusting us. We'll see you inside.
Finally! You know, you could've saved us both a lot of hassle if you'd just listened to us from the beginning.
Thanks for that, but I don't need lessons on honor from a ninja. Consider yourself lucky I'm in a good mood.
–Harumph!–
You know what? You look pretty cute when you're not trying to kill me.
What does the way I look have to do with anything?! Pfft! Arrogant samurai.
Actually, I'd prefer to let you live with the shame of your loss.
I feel the Kagehito clan owes you an apology for the rudeness of the reception at the front gate.
What's done is done, let's just put it behind us and move on. I'd like to discuss the fate of the shinobi team you dispatched on Shinmen's behalf.
Your friend purchased the skills of my clan several weeks ago. He suspected the lord of the Midori Ken was plotting to seize power.
So Daichi was behind it all along?
No. Quite the opposite, in fact.
Huh? But you just said --
Stop interrupting, Fumio. Let the Jonin speak.
Daichi, like Shinmen, possessed similar suspicions; he thought members of the shogun's court were plotting to stage a coup, and he was making moves to prevent such an event from taking place.

choice.text: Let's just get to the point.

dialogue.text: So if it wasn't Daichi behind the shogun's murder, who was it?
A veil of secrecy shrouds their movements, masking them from even our eyes.

But eventually, after weeks of searching, we learned that the plotters' activities were focused around a forest to the east. We suspected they were maintaining a hideout in the area, so I dispatched several of my most skilled shinobi to locate them.
Their disappearance two days ago adds weight to our theory that the conspirators are still at large within the forest.
So, to cut a long story short, how can I get my hands on the people responsible?
I will mark the location of the conspirators on your map. You may travel there yourself.
Chikako...
Sir!
You will make amends for your rash actions by escorting our friend to the team's last know location. Once done, you must find our lost clanspeople, and report back to me.
Sir!

choice.text: Heh heh! Me and Chikako... in the woods together...

dialogue.text: Chikako's a highly skilled kunoichi. I'm sure her abilities will come in useful.
Be about your business quickly, Chikako. Once you have finished with your duties in the forest, I will need you to bring Kurai back to our village.
Sir!
The Shira Tancho thanks your clan for your aid in this matter. We will ever remain in your debt.
Yeah, we couldn't have done it without you guys.
Your thanks are welcome but unnecessary. The Kagehito were merely fulfilling a contract between ourselves and your friend. We are loyal until our service ends.
Let's get moving.
Wait just a second! I don't think I like the idea of a stab-happy kunoichi following us around.
HEY! I'm NOT stab-happy!
Fine, but Chikako walks in front. I don't much fancy the idea of a knife in my back.
So, I suppose we can call this our first offical date. Right, Chikako?
Grrr! You really are one arrogant, self-absorbed, son of a –
Flattery will get you everywhere, Chikako. Confess your love to me while we walk.
Damn right you do! Your kunoichi nearly cut my head off!
Sir, I –
Silence, Chikako. Your continued impulsive actions bring great shame to our clan. You would do well to think before acting.
Sir!
Good! Now that's cleared up, how about telling us what you know about the shogun's murder?
If we're going to reach there in time, we need to get moving right away.
Ouch! Oh, I didn't you see there youngster. Sorry about that.
Heh heh... Hello traveler, it’s always nice to see a new face.
The name’s Kojuro the peddler. I travel between the towns buying and selling all sorts of – heh heh! – interesting items.
Please do drop by my stall when you have the time. I'm always happy to buy off any junk that you find on your travels.

choice.text: I am looking for the inn.

dialogue.text: Where can I find your stall?
Heh! Heh! Just head east along the main road and you'll see it.
Do you know where I can find the inn?
Looking to rest up or to just buy some food and drink for the road?
It's just right here behind me! Heh! Heh!
Nice talking to you, but I've got to run.
Heh! Heh! Look after yourself on the road, youngster!
It's dangerous to go alone. Take this.
The shinobi team was dispatched to the Kuniwashi territory. Chikako will help you locate them.
I'll find the lost shinobi.
I think you should know, the team you sent was wiped out with the exception of Kurai. He is safe and recuperating back at Masai Village. He is hurt, but should recover fully with rest.
Yes, Chikako informed me. I will dispatch a team to bring Kurai back to the village forthwith. We are in your debt, samurai. The mercy you exhibited has not gone unnoticed, be assured.
Watch out where you walk in here... we are nearing enemy territory. For a skilled ninja to pass undetected is a test enough, but for the likes of an untrained lout like you...

choice.text: I knew she cared for me!

dialogue.text: Then I'm glad you're with us, Chikako. Lead the way.
Are you all right, Chikako?
Y-yes, I'm fine... but we shouldn't linger.
Bah! Sneaking around is for cowards. If an enemy raises his head, I'll lop it off!
Tsk! Typical arrogant samurai, always trying to solve a problem with violence.
And I suppose you know a better way?
I know a thousand better ways!
Oh yeah? Well if it's all the same to you, I'll just stick to stabbing my enemy until it stops trying to kill me. Now let's go.
Is that concern I hear in your voice, Chikako? Don't worry, I won't leave you!
I wasn't –
Oh Chikako, your eyes confess what your lips cannot! You, too, feel the pull of our mutual attraction – I can tell!
Grrr! Why don’t you just shut... the hell... UP!
You find it difficult admitting your feelings; I understand. Let's leave it for now.
The trail ends here. We should be – oh!
Hanzo, Jiro, Hisao!
Looks like we found the missing Shinobi...
The wounds on their bodies are so precise. They were clearly slain by a master swordsman.
A master swordsman who’s probably still around...
I sure hope so. I feel like smashing some skulls!
My poor clanspeople... how I wish had been here to fight by your side. May your spirits find rest in the afterlife, my friends.
Someone who can take down an entire team of shinobi isn't a person we should underestimate.
My work here is done; I must report this discovery to my clan.
There're footprints here... a dozen or so... leading away to the north. Whoever did this, I expect they're somewhere close by.
I'll leave the rest to you.
Thank you for your assistance, Chikako. We wouldn't have made it this far without you.
You did as you were ordered. We'll handle things from here.
You're still here? Go on - scram!
Sorry, Chikako, for your clan's loss. What will you do now?
Quit your sniffling, Chikako. They're dead, you're alive; let's just move on.
D-do you guys feels that? It's the air. It feels damp, clammy – like the skin of a corpse...
Is that fear I hear in your voice, Fumio?
W-what?! N-no! I ain't afraid of nothing! I'm just saying... this place don't feel right.

choice.text: We're armed; there's nothing to worry about.

dialogue.text: Just hit the first thing that looks at you funny.
Hee hee! Aye-aye, sir!
Let's keep moving.
Feel free to wait outside, if you like.
What?! No way; I'm sticking with you guys.
Fumio, you go first.
– ! O-okay...

step.title: Find the plotters behind Masahiro's death

dialogue.text: Looks like this guy's the last of 'em!

choice.text: I'll give him one chance to surrender.

dialogue.text: You! Throw down your sword and tell us who killed the shogun, and we might just spare your life!
Uh, something tells me this guy ain't speechless with fear.
Be cautious! This man... he's not what he seems.
Here he comes!
Let's take him down!
Go on, beg for your life -- It won't do you any good.You're going to pay for murdering the Shogun!

step.title: Find the plotters behind Masahiro's death

dialogue.text: Is he dead?

Any excuse for a catch-up is fine by me.
Let's go.

step.title: Investigate the Silent Song at Yasuoka Town

dialogue.text: So Masahiro was murdered by Gojo Takamori, and Gojo Takamori's working with the Silent Song...

Hmm. This sure doesn't look like the kind of place they'd call home.
Yeah. I was expecting more dead things.
Ha! Be careful what you wish for!
Let's look around. I'm sure someone here knows something.
Maybe try the inn.
Your wine flask running low again, Satoshi?
What? Uh, no... I was just, umm... Trying to be helpful.
It's the, uh... most logical place to start.
Ahem!
Ha ha! You never change.
Any idea where we should start looking?
Gulp! S-samurai -- in my inn! Y-you're not part of Lord Takamori's army, are you?

choice.text: I'd never serve such a dishonorable master!

Phew! Well, ancestors be praised!

And what if we are?
B-because, uh... the drinks! Yes, the drinks are on the house, courtesy of his new loyal subjects!
Praise Lord Takamori!

Hey, it isn't nice to trick people, you know!

Praise Lord Ashikage!

choice.text: What does he know about the fighting between the clans?

Ah! I mean, uh... whose suffering I could be alleviating with food and drink from my inn.
Poor Lord Ashikage, he's such a good ruler. That Lord Takamori though, I've only heard bad things about him.
A cruel man, rotten to the core like a late summer's apple.
I hope Lord Ashikage teaches him a lesson, for all our sakes!
Aside from the clan wars, any other ... "strange" incidents in the area?
Yes, I haven't had a wine delivery in almost a week!
That's not just strange -- that's catastrophic!
I was thinking more along the lines of the, uh... "supernatural."
By my ancestors! Please, don't use language like that in here -- at least not while I still have paying guests!
Honestly, you're just like that old charcoal burner. He's always talking about the "spirits in the wood."
Why, he was in here not two nights ago, drinking and mumbling and frightening my customers with his ghost stories, the silly old fool. I sent him flying right through that door and onto his backside.
Huh! He can find another inn to haunt.

choice.text: I take it he's a skeptic.
We need to find the charcoal burner.

dialogue.text: So you don't believe in ghosts?
Oh, I believe in them just as much as any person who has lived through the Demon Wars.
But that doesn't mean I want to be reminded of it every five minutes by a sake-addled lunatic hoping to score free drinks from my customers.
We've got quite enough on our plates with the shogun dying and the Murasaki Tsuki invading, and the last thing any of us need is spook stories from an old hermit who should know better!
Leave the ghosts to their business, that's what I say!
Do you know where we can find this charcoal burner?
He lives in a hut to the south, right next to that forest he's so terrified of.
Honestly, you'd think he would've moved out by now; but no, he's still there. Bah! He's probably making the whole thing up.
And if he isn't... well, I'd rather not know about it, thank you very much!
What's in those woods can stay in those woods -- it doesn't need people like us riling it up and setting it loose.
Now if you don't mind, I've got paying customers to attend to. Good day.
Ancestors preserve me -- they're here!
I knew this day would come. I should've packed up and moved out a long time ago, but I was a stubborn old fool.
Well, I won't go down without a fight, I tells ya! My soul ain't no ordinary soul -- it's part raging tiger, part ferocious dragon!
I'll --

choice.text: Is he going to give me a chance to speak?
We're not here to harm him.

dialogue.text: Old guy, will you just shut up for a second?
Gulp! Y-yes, samurai-sama. Anything you say.
So who did you think we were?
Well, uh... I thought you were... "them". The fellows who live in that shrine in the -- gulp! -- h-haunted forest.
But you're not. I can see that now.

choice.text: What's so special about the shrine?
Does he know how to get to the shrine?

dialogue.text: What can you tell us about the strangers living in the shrine?
Huh! Not much, because I try to stay the hell away from them.
They wear masks, and long gray robes with hoods over their heads. They slip in and out of the forest every night or so...
... and that's when I hear the shrine bell being struck! Can't imagine what they're using it for... but I bet it ain't good.
There must be something significant about that shrine. What can you tell us about it?
Well, I know it was built to commemorate the warriors who died in a great battle in Yasuoka forest.
But the shrine's abandoned now; the priests who tended to it, they've gone elsewhere.
Too much blood fouling the soil.
Too many things that don't know they're dead.
"Things"? Like what, ghosts?
Call 'em Yurei, call 'em Demons, call 'em whatever you want. I don't know, I'm not a priest.
But I know they don't sleep easy in their graves any more, and I know those damned squatters in the shrine are responsible for waking 'em up
What can you tell me about the battle?
Oh, it was a long time ago now, during the Demon Wars.
The daiymos of a half dozen provinces put aside their differences and decided to do something about the mad man who caused the mess.
So they organized an army -- a big one!
There were footmen, archers, wagons, banners, and lots and lots of samurai in shiny armor!
Yep, I thought they were going to hand that sorcerer fella one hell of a pasting when they finally reached the capital.
But they never reached the capital, didn't even come close.
The sorcerer was waitin' for 'em, skulking the forest with an army of his own.
They ambushed the samurai, killed 'em all.
The dead samurai outnumbered the leaves on the trees.
It was a black day for the Empire.
Enough about that. Let's talk about something else.
So this shrine... do you think you could take us to it?
Gulp! Nope, not for all the tea, soft pillows, warm fires and full noodle bowls in the Empire!
I'm not eager to die, thank you very much!
Then how about giving us directions? I'm a scout, I'm sure I could find the place easily enough if you told us the way.
Now what possible reason could you have for wanting to visit that place? It's cursed -- or haven't you figured it out yet?
But fine, if that's what you want. I'll mark it on your map.
Now, I'm going to pack up my stuff and get the heck out of here. I'll be sure to say a prayer for your departed souls when I find a temple.

choice.text: Heh! He clearly doesn't know how good we are!

dialogue.text: Hey, we're the best damn samurai in the business, old guy! You'll see.
Sigh! Just don't say I didn't warn you!
You have nothing to fear. We'll get to the bottom of this mystery.
Please, we wish you no harm. We're here because we have some questions that need answering.
So you're not here to claim my immortal soul?
Phew! You had me worried there for a second.
This looks like the place.
Hmm... creepy lights, rolling mist, a smell of rot. Yeah, I'd say you're right, Mitsuo.
The soil, the trees, even the very air itself... all are poisoned with the taint of Yomi.
Huh! I can't wait to see what the locals are like!

Aim for the head. It's their weak spot.
I hope we haven't lost our touch.

It is just the calm before the storm, I fear.
We should be on our guard, the Silent Song will soon be aware of us.
Let's get to that shrine.

Gulp! Ain't no way I want to get lost in this place!

The place looks pretty run-down.

We'd better keep our weapons at the ready.

Here comes trouble!

intro.text: I have arrived at Yasuoka Forest in accordance with our plans.

The land here aches with the old wounds of battles long since fought. It seeps through the soil and flows through the boughs of the haggerd old trees, mingling with the blood of the dead who wilt upon the floor.
I cannot imagine a more suitable place to call home.
But now is not the time for quiet contemplation -- for I have work to complete! The Kanji ruins lie somewhere in the Cha Tonbo territory, and I must locate them for our allies.
Joy of Joys! Finally, after many months of futile searching and much expenditure of our cult's resources, I have finally located the Kanji ruins!

The vile Oni who inhabited the ruins are no more. I removed their taint, though the cost was considerable: twelve followers slain, several walking dead destroyed beyond resurrection. But I shall not dwell on their losses, for flesh is a resource the Silent Song possess in abundance

Instead, I will focus my mind on the next task: overcoming the magical barrier barring me from the ritual chamber. For while that barrier persists, the final stage of our Great Work cannot be undetaken.

The power of the Silent Song waxes strong in this forest now! The latest converts to our cause arrived yesterday, and they will aid me considerably as I seek to overcome the vexing magic of the Kanji and open the final door.

I have consulted what legend-scrolls I could find concerning that paltry sect of magicians, and I have discovered something that may be of use: apparently, in order to access the central chamber one must brandish a very specific object -- a dragon talisman. Furthermore, the scrolls state such talismans are commonly sealed inside 'other' shrines.
The prospect of hunting for more ruins in this backwater land is not one I welcome, yet it is a task I accept without complaint.

dialogue.text: Sheesh! What a load of horsecrap.

Indeed, but there is much within his tale that should cause us concern.

Bah! Jodai Hideaki might've known a trick or two, but I'm pretty sure surviving decapitation wasn't one of them.
Yeah, there's no way he could come back from the dead... right?

Eh -- ?
Sigh! I wish Hiroshi were here. He'd know what to do...
Heh heh...

Yeah... but how? We don't even know where he is.
The Kagehito might be able to locate him, but it will take time.

Sigh! Man, I'm just not cut out for this...
... heh heh heh...

... that's...

Hee hee! You really think so?

Ahem!

choice.text: That's the stupidest thing I've ever heard!

Well, I'd recommend trying to find those ruins you were talking about.
Hmm... kanji ruins... that reminds of of a tale I once heard.
Yes, they have too much in common to be just a coincidence.
Then spill the beans, Kojuro-san!
Sigh! So hasty. Always so hasty, you young people.
The tale mentions about a Kanji temple. Temple of the... oh, something or other. I can't quite remember now.

It's supposed to lie somewhere in Narimoto, concealed from the eyes of mortals by powerful magic!
The only clue as to its location lies with an ancient stone statue.
Do you have a map? Heh! Of course you have a map! Here, let me mark the statue's locations for you, and then you can visit it yourself.

An old, old sect... older than the great clans, older than the first Emperors. Heh! Older than the mountains themselves, some scrolls say.
No one knows what happened to them. Some say they traveled across the endless sea.
Heh! Just another mystery in need of answering.
This land's full of such mysteries, assuming you know where to look!
What should we do now?
We need to find those kanji ruins and get the dragon talisman. It's that simple.
The Cha Tonbo are brave fighters, and they will resist the Murasaki Tsuki advance for as long as they are able, I have no doubt.

Oh, and before I forget! I have a gift for you -- something that may come in useful.
Now where did I put it...
... Ah! Yes, here it is!

I don't know -- that's for you to figure out! But I'm certain they're important.

Or maybe there's some truth to it all?

Vist me at Kariya town when you have the chance. I look forward to hearing about your discoveries!
Oh yeah? Well, how about you just keep your nose out of other people's business?
Wait! If the Kojuro-san says he knows something, maybe we should hear him out?
Yeah, Kurai would be dead by now if it wasn't for that old guy's help.
So tell us what you know, Kojuro-san.
Ah, Kojuro-san! Sorry, we didn't see you there.

Hurry!

Ha ha! Oh don't worry. I'm only joking.
It's a little prank we like to pull on visitors from time to time, just to see their reaction.
That statue's perfectly safe, unless you're standing beneath it during a thunderstorm. Thing attracts lightning from all around.
See those scorch marks on the ground? They’re from the lightning bolts.
This statue looks old. How long has it been standing here?
Oh, he's been here for ages, through wind and hail, sun and storm... he's older than every person in this village put together.
Heck, he's older than the village itself!
The Cha Tonbo's lands are full of old ruins like this. There's nowhere else like it in the whole of the Empire.
There's an inscription on the base of the statue. Do you know what it means?
Ah, quite a puzzle, that one.
Some folks reckon it's a riddle of some kind, meant to lead a person to a valuable treasure.
Others claim it's just graffiti.
Shame the statue can't speak, eh? I'm sure he'd tell us what it all means!
Say, if you fellows are interested, you should visit the other statues in the territory.
Other statues...?
Yup! There are three of 'em in all, scattered around the countryside.
We came across one of the statues already, in the clearing not far from here.
Oh, then you have one more to find.
You got a map? Give me a second, I'll mark him down for you!
There!
Oh, and if you find any treasure, be sure to remember me, Yoji the farmer.
Now, I'd better get back to my crops.
Have fun on your treasure hunt!

intro.text: You learnt a new dragon dance step!
You learnt a new dragon dance step!

dialogue.text: That's all of them, then.
We should return to the Kanji monument.

step.title: Perform the kagura in front of the statue

dialogue.text: So we perform the dances in the order listed on the inscription, right?
It seems so, but tread lightly. We don't know the penalty for getting it wrong.
Magic, even the seemingly benevolent kind, can have powerful repercussions if not handled carefully.
Gulp! I don't like the sound of this, guys.
Then let's make sure we get the order right.

step.title: Perform the kagura in front of the statue

dialogue.text: Whoa!
Now that's how you hide a temple!
Illusion magic? Pah!
Just bury the damn thing -- nobody will find it then!
Yes, the magic of the Kanji is impressive indeed.
But the real test of our abilities begins now, I think.
So... who's going in first?

choice.text: It might be dangerous in there.

dialogue.text: What will we face inside?
The Kanji buried this temple because they did not want the secrets within falling into unworthy hands...
Doubtless there will be more perils awaiting us, and we should be prepared for anything.
Okay, I'll go first. But you guys had better be right behind me.
Like your shadow.
Yeah, we're with you, buddy.
That's one impressive statue!
Looks kind of out of place here, don't you think?
Yeah, but least it's not trying to kill us... unlike everything else in these ruins.
I wouldn't speak so soon, Satoshi.
-- Look!
I-it's... moving --?!
Me and my big mouth...
Here it comes!
Arms: check. Legs: check. Head: check.
Phew! At least we’re still in one piece.
Say, this armor... it's empty. Ain't nothing inside.
What the hell was that thing? It didn't look like something the Silent Song would conjure.
A guardian, placed in this temple to watch over the secrets of the Kanji.
Then at least we know the Silent Song haven't beaten us to the prize.
Let's search the area.
Huh? That looks like an old wine gourd.
Looks too big to be a wine gourd, Fumio.
Not if it belonged to that guy back there.
Heh! I'm beginning to like these Kanji fellas.
But... but where's the dragon talisman? I mean, wasn't that the whole point of coming here?
Hmm, I think we may have struck a problem...
Sigh! That's just great...
We traipse through miles of countryside, dodge a thousand spikey things falling from the ceiling of a crumbling old temple, fight for our lives against ancestors-knows-what...
... and all we get is a wine gourd.
Dammit! If Kojuro's led us on a wild goose chase... I'll wring his scrawny neck!
Then let's get out of here and find him. Didn't he say he'd be at Kariya village? I know how to get there. It isn't far.
I know a quick way to Kariya.
Soldiers, we have our orders!
General Magoichi has demanded we hunt down the warriors of the Cha Tonbo, and our scouts reported seeing a group flee to this village!
If those villagers won't hand the warriors over, we'll burn their hovels to the ground!
These Murasaki Tsuki spread like Itadori.
Yeah... And how do you handle knotweed in your garden, Yuudai?
I cut it down, of course.
Huh? Those are the ronin who attempted to slay our lord Takamori!
Men, kill them all -- and then we'll torch this village!
Your gardening skills have improved considerably, my friend.
That will be thanks to you, Yuudai. I took your words to heart, and I've been practising every opportunity I get.
Then when we have dealt with Takamori and I am back home again, I insist you help me with my harvest.
Consider it a deal, Yuudai. I'll gladly help you.
Guys, let's not start making our vacation plans just yet...
We still need to check up on Kojuro-san.
Maybe, Yuudai. We'll see.
I've always been pretty good at dealing with weeds, Yuudai. It's a gift.
Thank the ancestors for your intervention, samurai-sama. If not for your aid, those Murasaki Tsuki savages would have killed us all!
How did The Murasaki Tsuki manage to push this far east so quickly? Don't the Cha Tonbo have warriors in the field to stop them?
Oh, have you not heard? The Murasaki Tsuki have been overrunning the Cha Tonbo camps all over.
General Daisuke had led a force to stop them east of here, but the Cha Tonbo are desperately outnumbered.
You've got to hand it to Takamori... he sure knows how to plan a campaign.
If there is any compliment we can pay the man, that is surely the one.
Please, speak with the warriors at the inn. They will tell you more!
Has an old guy passed through here recently? He's a short fellow, bent over like an old willow tree. Name of Kojuro.
Ah. Yes, Kojuro-san is tending to the wounded soldiers at the inn.
A fine man, he has long been a friend to the people of this village.
We'll leave you to your business.
Let's go find Kojuro.
You will find Kojuro-san at the village inn, and he is tending to the wounded soldiers.
Eh?
Oh, my favorite band of ronin have returned -- and not a moment too soon!
Oooh... ouch!
There there, youngster. You just rest. I'll have you standing straighter than new bamboo in no time.
Now, where did I put that healing salve...
Kojuro-san, what's going on here? Who are all these men?
Ah... it's a sorry tale, youngster. They're rufugees and wounded from the Cha Tonbo Army stationed in Nagamiya.
As you can probably tell, the battle didn't go too well... Unless you happen to be one of the Murasaki Tsuki.
I arrived here as the first of the wounded were staggering through the gate, and I tried my best to save as many lives as I could.

intro.label: label1

dialogue.text: You'll be pleased to know that your story was true, Kojuro-san. We found the ruins, exactly where you said they'd be.
Well, we found "some" ruins.
Heh! My, that's a ray of sunshine in an otherwise glooming day!
So, what was it like inside?

choice.text: I never want to step into another ruin ever again!

dialogue.text: If I never see another Oni again it'll be too soon...
Heh! Those little fiends get everywhere! Still, I'm sure you dealt with them easily enough.

intro.label: label2

dialogue.text: Now, did you find anything else?
We did. What can you tell us about this...?

intro.text: You show Kojuro the Kanji gourd.

dialogue.text: Oh --!
This... this is stupendous...
... remarkable...
... fantastic!
Youngster, do you realize what you're holding?

choice.text: We don't have time for guessing games!

dialogue.text: Quit fooling around, Kojuro-san, and tell us already!

intro.label: label3

dialogue.text: This, youngster, is none other than the Sealing Gourd of legend; spoken of in fable, pondered upon by scholars for centuries...
... but never -- not until this moment -- gazed upon by mortal eyes.
And it is your key to ending all this madness!
So it wasn't a complete waste of time?
Heh! Far from it, young fella.
so, uh... this ain't the dragon talisman?
No -- but it's the next best thing!

No doubt Takamori has the Dragon Talisman in his clutches already, or at the very least knows where he can get it. Otherwise, why would he be marching his army through the Cha Tonbo lands with Masahiro's corpse in tow?
But this "gourd" is one of the few artifacts in existence with the power to stop him completing his ritual.
The ceremony to exorcise the Void Key will be long and elaborate, and it will require a specially consecrated location: another Kanji shrine, similar to the one you youngsters found.
That mad man's journal back in the forest mentioned he'd discovered another Kanji shrine, but it didn't say where.
Heh! No matter! Now that we have the Sealing Gourd, all we need to do is catch up to the Murasaki Tsuki army and use it to lock the Void Key away for all time!
Let's see how Takamori likes that!
Sigh! Kojuro-san, I'm not the kind of guy to go peeing in another man's sake bowl... but we tried attacking Takamori's camp before, and it didn't go too well.
Heh! Yes, but you didn't have me travelling with you last time!

choice.text: I'm glad to have Kojuro with us.

dialogue.text: Kojuro-san, you can't seriously be thinking of coming with us!
Yes -- I most certainly am! Do you think I'd let a bunch of freshly sprouted bamboo shoots like you tackle lord Takamori's army all by yourselves?
Fine, if you insist.

intro.label: label4

dialogue.text: Besides, we'll have the Cha Tonbo helping us, too
Uh... what, these guys here?
Tsk! No, not these men... General Daisuke and his troops!
General Daisuke still lives?
Heh! Yes... but for how long is dependent on us.
General Magoichi, one of lord Takamori's commanders, is attacking his armies at Nagamiya even as we speak.
General Daisuke is lion-brave and loyal to his daimyo, and not even Takamori can dismiss the threat posed by the Cha Tonbo while he remains alive.
Indeed! Daisuke still has most of the Cha Tonbo army under his command. It's not enough to defeat the Murasaki Tsuki one-on-one, but it will be enough to help us find Takamori.
Kojuro-san, you cunning old rooster ...
I'm impressed!
Heh! Well, you don't get to my age without learning how to use your brain.
Now, you youngsters give me a minute to collect my belongings and check these warriors' injuries, then we'll make a start for the Cha Tonbo camp in Nagamiya.
No way -- you're staying right here. The last thing we need is your old bones rattling around behind us.
Hey! My bones might be old, but they're infused with a lifetime of wisdom! You'll do well to remember that, youngster!
I mean no offense, Kojuro-san, but you are a venerable elder of no mean age, and we will be going into combat...
Heh! Don’t worry your head about me, youngster. I know how to look after myself.
Kojuro-san, your help will be invaluable.
Uh, well... I was hoping you'd tell me, Kojuro-san.
Traps, mainly. Stabby traps, slashy traps, crushy traps... you know, the usual.
Heh! Yes, I thought there would be.
Wait a sec'... you knew about the traps but didn't bother to warn us?!
Oh... didn't I? I could have sworn I did... Heh! That'll be old age catching up with me!
The important thing to remember is that you survived it, and you'll be stronger for the experience, I'm sure.
Not something I want to repeat in a hurry, I'll tell you that much!
Heh heh! Yes, the Kanji never were known for their hospitality.
I have marked the route through the haunted forest.
If we follow the markings while travelling at full speed, we should be able to reach the shrine without incident.

option.text: Fast travel through the Haunted Forest?

dialogue.text: Well, that wasn't quite the answer I was hoping for.
Ghosts in the forest and the Silent Song running about in the countryside? This sounds too convenient to be just a coincidence, Mitsuo.
I suppose you're right. We'd better check this guy out.
Say, uh... Mitsuo.
How's, uh... your wife and son getting on?
Haruka and Matsu are good. Matsu's four now -- can you believe that?
Heh! He fired his first arrow the other day -- hit the target from forty paces, one shot!
Hee hee! That little tyke's gonna grow up to be a marksman just like his dad!
What about Haruka's sister? How is she doing?
Mizuki? She's good.
She, uh... she ever talk about me?
No... why?
Oh, no reason.
Hee hee! Nice try there, Satoshi!
I applaud your subtlety, Satoshi.
Sigh! Well, it was worth a shot.
If the old guy's directions are right, we should reach the start of the forest if we head south.
Huh! And then the fun begins...
Uh... what was that girl's name again, Mitsuo? You know, the cute one who works in your village's inn?
Izumi?
Hee hee! Yeah... Izumi.
She still single?
I think so... but you're better off leaving her alone, Satoshi, especially after last time.
Oh, man... she still remembers?
You were naked and peeing in the village well... everybody remembers.
Sigh! Talk about holding a grudge ...
Hee hee hee! You clown, Satoshi!
My, my... what a sorry state these men are in.
Look at their faces... that's defeat right there.
Yeah, the Murasaki Tsuki sure pulled a number on them.
At last! Look, Madoka, reinforcements!
What, four ronin and an old guy?
Well, let's grab our swords and go kill us some Murasaki Tsuki!
Huh! I don't think so.

choice.text: Are these the only warriors left?
Get to the point and ask about General Daisuke.

dialogue.text: Soldier, what happened to you?
Huh! Isn't it obvious?
The Murasaki Tsuki happened.
They came from the east less than a day ago, drums beating and banners flapping in the wind; an entire army, many thousands strong.
The ground shook as they drew closer, and that's when we saw them... saw the advanced troops.
At first we thought they were survivors fleeing the fighting... they wore the same brown livery as us, only bloodstained and torn...
But it wasn't until they came closer that the truth was revealed...
Heads carved in half like watermelons... stomachs burst open like leaking wine sacks...
These weren't the survivors -- they were the casualties!
Takamori had resurrected the corpses of our comrades!
We thought our days were numbered for sure, that we'd end up like our friends... shuffling undead in the vanguard of Gojo Takamori's army.
But the Murasaki Tsuki weren't interested in fighting us... they had bigger fish to fry.
They headed north, in the direction of the Cha Tonbo castle!
We've been here ever since.
Are you men the only survivors?
We're the only men capable of standing on our own two feet unaided, that's for sure.
The wounded were sent to Kariya in the west; the rest of us stayed here, as were our orders.
But we're useless as a fighting force now. We haven't been resupplied for days, and we're close to collapse through hunger and fatigue.
The reason we don't leave our posts is because we don't have the energy to move.
And what of your commander? Is he still alive?
We're not... we're not too sure.
The main Cha Tonbo army is encamped north of here.
But there's hundreds of Murasaki Tsuki troops between them and us, and more enemy troops flooding into the territory as we speak.
If the Murasaki Tsuki have caught General Daisuke unawares, the army's days are surely numbered...
Sigh! Well, there's nothing we can do about it now except pull out and head to Kariya.
We should just thank our ancestors we made it out of there alive.
So you would rather retreat than rescue your comrades? Cowards! you dishonor the sacrifice of Cha Tonbo!
We know we're cowards...
You can’t make us feel any worse about ourselves than we already do...
Then fight, damn it!
Pick up your swords, dust yourselves down, and get back out there!
B-but...
You could be the difference between victory and defeat for the Cha Tonbo.
Yeah, you can't chicken out now! Your clan ain't quiters, everyone knows that!
They're right, Madoka-san. We have to fight, or else our clan's finished!
Sigh! You shame us with your bravery, ronin.
We'll gather our weapons and our courage, and we'll travel to General Daisuke's camp.
Heh heh! Quite an inspiring speech you youngsters made.
Now, let's go find the rest of the Cha Tonbo!
Then tell me where General Daisuke is. Maybe there's something we can do to help him.
The Cha Tonbo Command HQ is located directly north of here.
You ronin must be insane if you think you can help him.
Insane? Yeah, it's been said before.
But we've been through worse and survived, and now isn't the time to change old habits.
Huh! I wish I had your attitude.
Well, good luck to you all. We'll pray for your success.
And for your souls.

step.title: Head to Cha Tonbo Command HQ

dialogue.text: The Murasaki Tsuki are attacking again! Warriors of the Cha Tonbo -- protect your commander!
Slay all the Cha Tonbo weaklings!
The Cha Tonbo need your help, youngster!
huff! We owe you our -- puff! -- lives, samurai. Alas, I feel your heroics may have earned you the same fate as the rest of us -- death at the edge of a Murasaki Tsuki blade!
We're here to aid the Cha Tonbo. Please, tell us where we can find General Daisuke.
The commander suffered a grevious injury when the Murasaki Tsuki attacked. His bodyguard pulled him from the press of combat, and now he is in the center of our camp, to the north.
Thank the heavens he's still alive! Let's go find him!
The Murasaki Tsuki are retreating.
If I may ask, to whom do the Cha Tonbo owe their thanks?

choice.text: We're just a band of humble ronin.

dialogue.text: We're just a band of humble ronin, Daisuke-sama. These warriors who travel with me are Shira Tancho Old Guard.
I have heard the tales of Old Guard prowess in battle. Many within the Empire have forgotten the sacrifices made by the Shira Tancho during the Demon Wars, but not I.
The Old Guard stand with you, Daisuke-sama. We are here to help you defeat the Murasaki Tsuki.
Then in the name of my Lord Ashikage, I thank you.

choice.text: What's the state of his army?

dialogue.text: Daisuke-sama, how many warriors remain with you?
Two thousand warriors marched with me... less than half that number remains now.
Many are wounded, and all are suffering from exhaustion. But we are the Cha Tonbo, and this is our land.
We will fight to the last drop of blood to see Takamori's army defeated.
Daisuke-sama, what can we do to help?
The Murasaki Tsuki have us boxed in.
Like a noose around a condemned man's neck, their grip tightens with every passing moment. The situation is desperate, I cannot lie.
We're the Shira Tancho Old Guard, Daisuke-sama. Desperate situations are our speciality!
In particular, the western and southern postions are severely depleted, and they are certain to fall in the next Murasaki Tsuki attack.
Then we know what we need to do, right guys?
We should hold the line and drive the Murasaki Tsuki back.
I will defend the southern side of the camp. You warriors can --
Eh --?! Oh no you will not, Daisuke-sama! In case you haven't noticed, you've taken an arrow to the knee!
I can patch you up, have no fear of that. But you won't be walking any time soon, and certainly not doing any fighting!
What --?! But I must fight! My duty is to --
Your duty is to win this war and protect the Cha Tonbo's lands, and you won't do that if you fall in battle.
An army without a general is like a chicken without a head; it'll run about for a while, but it'll fall over soon enough.
No, you'll stay here. These youngsters can handle the fighting.
Painful though it is to admit... I suppose your words make sense. Fine, I will leave the defense of the camp to the ronin.
Heh! Don't worry, Daisuke-sama. We won't break anything!
Yuudai, you and I will take the south entrance. Fumio, you and our friend can take the west.
Count me in, Satoshi. I'm ready!
They won't pass while I live, you have my word.
Mitsuo, you stay mobile and shoot any Murasaki Tsuki that slip by us. Teach those bastards a lesson they won't forget.
Got it, Satoshi. I have more than enough arrows to go round.
We won't let you down, Daisuke-sama.
So this is the vaunted spirit of the Shira Tancho? Truly, you do justice to the legend.
You can sing our praises after we've won this battle, Daisuke-sama. For now... let's just get to our postions!
Ah, the reckless bravery of youth! You youngsters look after yourselves, you understand?
Is this such a good idea, Satoshi? I mean, five of us against an entire army?
Heh! I know... I almost feel sorry for the Murasaki Tsuki.
Hee hee! We'll give 'em a chance to surrender, don't worry.
I am an unbeatable warrior, general Daisuke. These men traveling with me, they're the Shira Tancho Old Guard.

step.title: Head to the Western perimeter of the camp

dialogue.text: Halt! You're not a member of the Cha Tonbo army!
We are for this battle, friend. General Daisuke sent us to fight alongside you.
Then you can guard the western entrance with us, it won't be long before the Murasaki Tsuki --
The enemy are here! Battle positions!
Looks like we arrived just in time!

step.title: Head to the Western perimeter of the camp

dialogue.text: Thank the ancestors you arrived when you did, samurai. I don't think we would have held them back without --
The enemy have broken through the eastern perimeter!
Damn Murasaki Tsuki rats and their tunnels!
Buddy, get to the eastern edge of the camp and hold 'em off. I'll stay here and help these guys out!

step.title: Head to the Eastern perimeter of the camp

dialogue.text: You creeps keep charging forward if you want to. I've got enough arrows for everybody!
You enjoying yourself, Mitsuo?
Huh! Like eating sweet rolls at a harvest festival, friend.
But here, you take over. I'll protect Kojuro-san and Daisuke-sama as they withdraw north!
Meet me to the north entrance as soon as you're finished with these guys!

step.title: Head to the North Entrance of the camp

dialogue.text: Damn Murasaki Tsuki sure don't know when to quit!
Phew! Thanks for the assist back there, Kojuro. That Murasaki Tsuki almost got the better of me.
You don't get to my age by letting your guard down!
The Murasaki Tsuki have broken through the eastern perimeter! We need archers over there!
Sigh! No rest for the wicked, eh?
Friend, you protect General Daisuke and Kojuro-san while I defend the east.
I'll see you later.
That one sure is --
Enemy troops sighted to the north!
Protect the General!
Thanks for the help, friend! We'll stay here to guard the General. Please aid our comrades in the east!
Go on! We can manage here!

step.title: Head to the Eastern perimeter of the camp

dialogue.text: Mitsuo!
Guess this means I'll be fighting you next.
You slew my friend, Magoichi. I'll make you --
Pay for what I've done?
Yeah, yeah, I know the line. I hear it all the time.
Say... Aren't you that ronin who tried killing Lord Takamori back at our camp?
So this guy here, was he one of your Shira Tancho buddies too?
Yes, and his name was Mitsuo. He was worth a thousand of you murdering Murasaki Tsuki.
Old Guard, eh? Man, I'm a little disappointed. I mean, I thought the Shira Tancho were supposed to be invincible.
I hope you last longer than your friend!
You won't get lucky again, Magoichi.
Lucky? What, you think that was some kind of fluke?
Friend, I could kill guys like that in my sleep. I'm the Slashing Claws of the Gray Wolf, or haven't you heard?
Whoa -- color me impressed!
You're actually not too bad with a sword, you know that?
Still, I've got a job to do, so that means I'm going to have to end this little sparing session and get serious.
Apologies.
Not so fast!
Sorry for the delay. We would've gotten here sooner, but those Murasaki Tsuki just don't know when to --
Look -- Mitsuo's hurt!
Mitsuo!
GRRR--! No one harms one of our pals and gets away with it!
Man, you wait all your life for a Shira Tancho to turn up, and then four come along at once.
I've got to admit though... I'm not impressed by what I've seen so far.
The way Takamori-sama talks about you, I thought you guys were going to be made of bronze.
But it turns out you bleed just like the rest of us.
We'll shut your fool mouth up for good, you cold-blooded bastard!
Heh! Let's see what you've got!
Magoichi-sama! Our lord has issued the order for you to withdraw immediately!
Withdraw --?! But I was just getting started here!
He demands your presence at his side at once. We have broken through the Cha Tonbo castle's inner walls. It is time to move on to the next phase of the plan.
Damn! Well, orders are orders, I suppose. And a good samurai always obeys his orders.
You Shira Tancho try not to die before I find you, okay?
That bastard got away!
Hnng ...
Mitsuo! Man, you're still alive!
Looks like I was wrong... I didn't have enough arrows after all.
Hold on buddy, we'll get you some help!
T-too late for me now, Fumio...
The wound -- Cough! Cough! -- it's too deep.
W-what, this little cut here?
Bah! It's... it's just a scratch, nothing to worry about.
Kojuro-san will have something to fix you up with, I'm sure of it.
You always were a terrible liar, Satoshi.
Mitsuo...
It doesn't matter, though. I'm ready for it... for the end.
Hey, when did you become such a quitter, Mitsuo? Please, buddy, you gotta keep fightin' a little while longer.
Sniff! I mean, think of Matsu and Haruka. They're waitin' for you back home, at the farm.
You can't disappoint 'em!
Fumio... let him go.
B-but...
Summer turns to winter, fruit withers on the vine... and all men die eventually.
Give Mitsuo the dignity his bravery deserves.

choice.text: There must be something we can do!

dialogue.text: Yuudai-san, how can you be so cold? This man's your comrade -- we must aid him!
Yuudai's right, friend. Me, I'm f-finished... the other guys, they know it too... they're just too scared to admit it.
We've seen enough men die in front of us to know what the end looks like...
But I have a favor to ask, from one friend to another... it's a small request, but it will mean a lot to me...
Name it, Mitsuo, and we'll do it -- you have our word.
Take my bow... to my son... tell him that he's to practice with it... every day... just like his dad -- cough! -- taught him.
I want him to grow up to be big and strong... so that he can protect his mother and watch over the farm...
As for Haruka, tell her that I love her, and that she will always be able to find me... under the cherry blossom tree... where we spent our first evening together...
We'll pass the message on, pal. I swear it.
On our oaths as Shira Tancho warriors, Mitsuo, and as your friends.
Sniff! You'd better believe it, buddy.
It was good to travel... with you guys... again...
Sniff! Poor Mitsuo...
May his soul find rest in the afterlife.

choice.text: Now isn't the time to mourn.

dialogue.text: Mitsuo stood his ground and fought till the end. He was a fine samurai.
That bastard Takamori... we owe him for this.
If there is any justice in this world, Satoshi, then he will receive payment in kind very soon, have no fear.
Just so long as we're the ones dealing it out.
Let's go to the north section of the camp to tell General Daisuke that the Murasaki Tsuki have pulled back. I'm sure he'll have a new mission for us.
As for Mitsuo... we'll bury him in the forest, somewhere he won't be disturbed.
Sniff! I'll take his bow like he asked. After we've killed Takamori, let's pay Haruka a visit, break the bad news.
We need to put this behind us and move on. Takamori still has an army out there, and we need to stop him from completing the ceremony.
Yuudai-san's right, Fumio. There's nothing we can do...
D-damn it all!
We've seen enough men die in front of us to know what the end looks like, Fumio.

step.title: Head to the North Entrance of the camp

dialogue.text: The Murasaki Tsuki have retreated. I take it this is your handiwork?
It was... but we lost Mitsuo.
Ah, poor Mitsuo-san. He was a fine young man and a good soul, I could tell.
His actions saved the Cha Tonbo from certain disaster today, and he will be remembered as a hero to our clan, small solace though it may be to you.
No, that means a lot. Mitsuo was brave and honorable, just like a samurai should be.
So, what's your next move, Daisuke-sama?
I must rally what remains of my army, and then we will march back to our castle and lend what aid we can.
Then count us in, Daisuke-sama. We’ve got a few scores to settle with Gojo Takamori.
Gladly, my friend. Your service to the Cha Tonbo Clan is immeasurable, and it will be an honor to fight alongside you all.
I will lead my warriors to our Command HQ at Atsuzawa. We can discuss our next move there.
I'll travel with General Daisuke's army and meet you at Atsuzawa soon.
And don't worry about Mitsuo. I'll make sure he's given a proper burial.
It looks like the Murasaki Tsuki are doing some digging here.

Travel to the Command HQ at Atsuzawa

dialogue.text: Ah, the saviors of the Cha Tonbo have arrived.
My scouts have just returned from their reconnisance duties. Your presence is sorely needed.
So, what did they discover?
The news is grave... as I feared it would be.
Our castle has fallen and the defenders within wiped out. No one was spared in the Murasaki Tsuki assault.
But how could a castle fall to Takamori's troops so quickly?
Only one man is capable of bringing an entire fortress to its knees in such a short space of time.
General Yohei, the second of Lord Takamori's three field commanders, is a master of siege craft.
He is a brutal, unrefined weapon, but his skills at laying siege to a fortress are not easily countered.
Daisuke-sama, we came here to fight, not to talk. Tell us what to do -- and we'll get to it.
Yeah, I'm tired of kicking my heels out here. Let us at the enemy, Daisuke-sama!
There will be foes aplenty soon enough, my courageous friends. But first I must explain our plan of attack:
The Murasaki Tsuki assault was swift and absolute, and the walls remain intact and the gate has been repaired. A direct assault against it will be folly.
But we Cha Tonbo know every stone of that castle's walls, and there are secrets concealed within that not even Lord Takamori has been able to discover.
Such as?
Such as the culvert that lies within the western wall. It is hidden beneath undergrowth and difficult for outsiders to spot.
The culvert serves to channel the water that runs from the mountains during late spring. It will be empty during this time of year, and it is large enough to accommodate a small party of warriors.
And that's where we come in, right?
Correct. By entering the castle via the culvert, the four of you will be able to locate the castle flag room and open the castle gate.

Reaching the culvert will require you to pass through a small warren of caves in the forest to the north. It is a dangerous route; the caves are occupied by Oni. But it will prevent the Murasaki Tsuki from catching sight of you.
And once we are inside the castle?
After that, you will need to scale the Castle Inner Walls. I will supply you with a portable ladder for the purpose.
Hmm... an audacious plan, Daisuke-sama. But much rests on the efforts of just a handful of warriors.
Hey, not just a handful of warriors, Yuudai! We're the Old Guard, remember?
Yeah, the best damned samurai around!
I ask a lot of you, I know this. But you defied General Magoichi and routed the Murasaki Tsuki.
No warrior under my command could hope to match your skills.

choice.text: The Murasaki Tsuki must pay for what they've done.

dialogue.text: For Mitsuo, for the Cha Tonbo, and for all who have suffered at the hands of Takamori, we'll help you retake your castle, Daisuke-sama.
On behalf of the Cha Tonbo Clan, I thank you all.
The cave entrance is located within the forest directly east of the town. Travel there and fight your way through the Oni until you come out within the Castle Town.
After that, find the culvert, enter the castle, and locate the flag room. My troops will be concealed a short distance outside the castle town, awaiting the signal to attack.
I'll wait here with the General, too. I'm not the age for scampering over castle walls.
Then the time for planning has passed, Daisuke-sama. We'll be on our way.
Our hopes rest on your courage, samurai.
Good luck.
Okay, Okay... enough with the compliments already. We'll do it. Quit your sniffling.
You samurai... you move with the grace of an avalanche.
It's good to see you again, Chikako. Why are you here?
To help you, of course.
I thought you might need my skills. I mean, Infiltration is hardly your strong suite.
Ha ha! You didn’t come here to see a certain special someone, by any chance?
I-I don’t know what you’re talking about! I’m here b-because, uh...
because my jonin says I needed the practice!
Yes, I'm here to practice my castle infiltration technique!
Riiiight...
Grrr...!
Y-you samurai... you’re lucky I’m helping you. I could leave, you know? I could leave you all to it, see how long you last without my help.
Whoa there -- calm down! I was only joking!
Huh! Your sense of humor leaves much to be desired, do you know that?

choice.text: I think we make a great couple!

dialogue.text: I value your skills, Chikako. I'm honored to have you fighting alongside us.
And... and I respect your skills, too.
Besides, your friend -- Hiroshi, was it? -- sent a message to my village. He wishes you to know "the young master" is safe.
Hiroshi and the shogun's heir are safe?!
Ha ha ha! That's the best news I've heard since this whole damned war started!
With Lord Masahiro's son safe, a future yet remains for our clan.
Once we've killed Takamori and had our revenge, we should track 'em down.
All the Old Guard -- together again!
Except for Mitsuo, that is...

choice.text: How did she know we were here?

dialogue.text: How did you know where to look for us?
I'm a ninja -- or did you suddenly forget? I can track anyone... if I want to.
Besides, I listened to your conversation with General Daisuke.
The plan he proposed sounded feasible... if he employed ninja to do it.
But he didn't... he employed you. And you possess all the subtlety of a herd of wild oxen.
It would be a shame to let you die after the effort my clan has been through to keep you alive.
So I waited here, concealed, until I heard you approach.
Then let's get moving. I take it you'll be leading the way, Chikako?
Naturally! I am trained in the ways of infiltration after all.
Follow me!
I don't need your help, Chikako. But I'll accept it... for now.
Huh! And I ask for nothing more than that, samurai.
Once all this is over, let's get a little hut together in the woods somewhere! It'll be soooo romantic!
Sigh! You're extremely annoying, even for a samurai.
And you're delusional.
It's really quite pitiful.
You just can't stop interfering, can you?
I'm just doing my duty, that's all.
Oh, Chikako! My heart soars on wings of love every time I see you!
Don't get any ideas, samurai. I'm here to aid you with your mission -- nothing more.
So that's the front gate... think we should knock?
Not without a battering ram, Satoshi.
Tsk! You samurai, always thinking with your swords and never with your heads.
We should stick to General Daisuke's plan and find that cave. Anything else is suicide.
Here's the entrance to the Oni Cave. Keep on your guard!

dialogue.text: Man, look at the size of that guy!
A Red Oni... they're dangerous. Too dangerous for the five of us to handle, that's for sure.
So we what, try another route?
No. We sneak past it. Red Oni are fearsome creatures, but they're easily lulled into sleep.
We must simply bide our time and wait for it to doze off, and then we can move.
Simple, no?
Gulp! If you say so.

step.title: Enter the Castle Town using the Oni Caves

dialogue.text: Didn't I tell you it would be simple?
The exit is up ahead. Let's keep moving.

step.title: Enter the Castle Town using the Oni Caves

dialogue.text: Wait--!
Good. We haven't been spotted.
So, what is your plan?
Uh... Plan?
Yes, your plan for reaching the Castle Flag Room. What is it?
We, uh... didn't really come here with a plan.
Small details aren't our strong point, you see.
We're more "big picture" guys.
So your intentions were to what, storm the castle with swords swinging and voices raised, hoping to fight your way through the Murasaki Tsuki?
That's about the size of it, yeah...
Sigh! You clearly didn't learn your lesson from last time, then.
Honestly, I'm amazed you have survived this long
Hee hee! Not as amazed as us!
Then it's lucky for you that I showed up when I did.
I have a plan, and it's guaranteed to work.
Oh? Then tell us, because we're all ears.
First we should make our way to the Western side of the Outer Walls where General Daisuke mentioned the hidden culvert is.
After going through the culvert, wait for me while I scout out a safe route into the Castle Courtyards.
The courtyards should be heavily guarded so stick close to me and we'll make our way into the castle under the cover of shadows.
Once in, I'll head to the Castle Flag Room with one of you while the rest guard the stairs in case any Murasaki Tsuki turn up.
Your opinions?
Say, that's not half bad!
Sure sounds good to me.
We bow before your superior wisdom.

choice.text: it's certainly better than our plan.

dialogue.text: That's an excellent plan, Chikako.
Good. We're in full agreement, then.
Do as I do, move when I move, step where I step... and we should make it to the Castle Flag Room in one piece.
Thanks but no thanks, Chikako. That "plan" has suicide written all over it.
Tsk! Fine. Then suit yourself.
I'll just leave you all to it...
Hey! Let's not be too hasty there, friend.
Chikako's plan is pretty solid, and I think we should follow her advice, at least for now.
Pretty solid --?!
It's foolproof -- I guarantee it.
Huh! It's even Samurai-proof!
Brains as well as beauty! Never has there been a more perfect being than you, Chikako!
Sigh! A simple "yes, I agree" would have sufficed.
Hmm... the culvert should be around here somewhere.
There are lots of bushes. How will we know which one to search?
Just leave it to me to find, samurai. My senses are as sharp as a razor bl --
Hey, guys! I think I found it -- over there, behind that bush!
Ha ha! Chikako, meet Fumio! His senses are as sharp as a rock's!
Hee hee! Stone beats razor any day, right?
Huh! Beginner's luck, that's all.
Hey, I'm eagle-eyed Fumio, or didn't you know? Nothing gets past me!
It's true. Fumio has an uncanny knack for noticing things out of the ordinary. No one's quite sure how he does it.
Then I suppose the old adage is true; there really is no fooling a fool.
Hee hee! Damn right!
Hey! wait just a minute...

intro.text: You found the hidden culvert!
